newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes unmoved in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes unmoved in slack trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved in lethargic trade on Friday which saw little demand for either dollars or rupees, dealers said.
The rupee close at 56.60 to the dollar after opening slightly weaker at 56.62 and hovering around that level for much of the day, they said.
"There was no genuine import covering. No big bills in the market," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer. "People are also reluctant to hold plus positions due to volatile call rates."
Call money rates went up to a high of 23 percent and down to a low of 17 percent before closing at 18 percent, dealers said.
"State banks were borrowing, but there was enough liquidity in the market to keep money rates from going up," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
Rates began dropping earlier this week after reaching a high of 30 percent earlier this month.
On Friday, the Central Bank pushed up the dollar by two local cents in response to its overseas gains against the yen and mark, setting buying and selling rates at 56.0018 and 57.1332.
